stamp: {"keys":[{"id":"k","problem":"The column 'נכסים בסוף ספטמבר' does not say it means the money pooled in the track; it reads as the fund's own assets.","where":"that column's head","kind":"general"}],"liked":[]}

raised: The page doesn't say which track suits someone their age (61)
Not sure who 'רשות שוק ההון' is
The '123 מקור 123 מחושב 123 הזנתה' line is confusing: 123 of what?
The orange 'not updated since September' warning worried them, and seems overdone for one-month-old data
Didn't understand the track types 'עוקב מדדים - גמיש' and 'הלכה איסלאמית'
The main table is too long; they scrolled 7 screens hunting for כללי in each company
The past-returns note ('לפני דמי הניהול ולפני מס') is at the bottom but should be at the top
Don't know what's inside 'חוקים וכללים · 7'
Dotted underlines under numbers aren't recognisable as clickable
The sort arrows next to column titles went unnoticed
'פחות מ־3 שנים' is unclear; a plain 'track is too new' would be better
'מניות 101%' makes no sense: how can it be more than 100%?
Unclear whether 'מט"ח 99%' is a risk for them
Same company has two tracks with the same name (e.g. two מניות at Harel); which one would they be in?
Unclear whether the fees shown are what they'd pay or can be negotiated
No cost in shekels (e.g. on 100,000 ₪ this costs X a year)
No returns after fees; they had to subtract the fee themselves
No tax information on withdrawal or the age-60 annuity option
No plain-language risk measure, such as the worst-year drop
No information on how to withdraw money, how fast, or the penalty
No minimum deposit or how-to-open information
No information on moving between companies without tax
Would drop the round coloured charts
Would drop the מההפקדה line, since it's almost always 0%
Would drop or move the קופה number column
Would hide Ayalon and new tracks that have no data
Would hide the other product buttons once a product is chosen

problems.why: The reader used the assets column and read it correctly as money in the track ('6.7 מיליארד ₪ in the track'), so they never raised the problem of it looking like the fund's own assets.
